title: Quiz: Predictions and Residuals with modelr

questions.text: What does data_grid(x) do when x is a continuous variable with values 1–10?
options: Returns only the unique observed values of x from the dataset
Creates a new data frame with a single evenly spaced sequence of x values spanning the observed range
Generates a random sample of x values from a normal distribution
Subsets the original dataset to rows where x is an integer
questions.explanation: data_grid() creates an evenly spaced prediction grid over the range of each specified variable. For integer x = 1:10, it returns one row per unique value.

questions.text: add_residuals(sim1_mod) computes which quantity for each row?
options: The observed y minus the predicted ŷ
The Cook's distance for each observation
questions.explanation: A residual = observed y − predicted ŷ. add_residuals() adds this as a new column (named 'resid' by default) to the original data frame.

questions.text: If the residuals-vs-predictor plot shows a perfectly random cloud of points centred at zero, you should try adding more predictors to improve the model.
questions.explanation: Random scatter around zero is the ideal outcome — it means the model has captured all systematic variation. Adding predictors is only warranted if residuals show a pattern (curve, fan shape, or non-zero mean).

questions.text: You fit a model and add_residuals() to a dataset. The residuals form a fan shape — small spread at low x, large spread at high x. What assumption is violated?
questions.explanation: A fan shape in residuals indicates heteroscedasticity — the variance of the residuals is not constant across predictor values. OLS assumes constant variance (homoscedasticity).

questions.text: add_predictions() works with 'any model that has a predict() method'. What does this mean in practice?
options: It only works with lm() models
It can be used with glm(), gam(), rpart(), and other model types, not just lm()
It requires the model to be re-fitted before adding predictions
It returns predictions only for the training data, not new observations
questions.explanation: add_predictions() calls predict(model, newdata = ...) internally. Since glm(), gam(), rpart(), and many other R model objects have a predict() method, add_predictions() works with all of them.
